children: Greece's finance ministry announced on Wednesday its medium-term fiscal plan, which projects public debt falling to 110% of gross domestic product by 2030, supported by strong economic growth, primary fiscal surpluses and early bailout loan repayments.
Here are the key economic projections:
Debt is projected to fall to 128.5% of GDP in 2027, 121.3% in 2028, 115.2% in 2029 and 110.1% in 2030
Economic growth is seen at 2.3% in 2027, easing to 2.1% in 2028 and 2029 and to 2.0% in 2030
The primary surplus, which excludes debt-servicing interest costs, is projected at 3.2% of GDP in 2027 and 3.0% of GDP in 2028, 2029 and 2030
